title: Staff against pupils
question: As enrolment fell, which kinds of staff grew and which shrank?
finding: Between 2014-15 and 2024-25 pupils in San Francisco public schools fell 4% while all staff went from 6,387 to 6,693 full-time-equivalents (+5%), or 108 to 118 per 1,000 pupils. Grew: all other staff +24%; classroom aides +3%. Shrank: school administrators -36%; office support staff -11%; teachers -3%; district administrators unchanged. The State's own file, 2019-20 to 2024-25, shows the same direction: pupils -9%; teachers -14%; administrators -35%; pupil-services staff -46%; other staff +66%.
how: Full-time-equivalent staff by category as the State reported them to the federal Common Core of Data, summed over every public-school unit located in San Francisco (the district, the county office and charter schools), divided by the pupils of the same units and shown per 1,000 pupils. "All other staff" is the total less the five named categories; it includes counsellors, librarians, pupil-support and other support staff, whose own columns are not reported consistently. The last four columns are the State education department's separate count for the district with the charter schools it authorised.
limits: These counts are only as good as the State's reports: categories were redefined in 2020-21, one year is missing and one teacher figure is plainly out of line. Staff paid by outside contractors are not counted, and the files do not say whether charter-school staff were in the district's figures before 2018-19, when their pupils were; if they were not, the early years understate staff per pupil. More aides and support staff per pupil can follow from more pupils with disabilities, which the State fiscal-crisis team says rose here while enrolment fell. A district where living costs are high must pay more to hire and keep staff, and one with many small schools, or with many pupils who are learning English, have disabilities or are poor, will spend more per pupil for honest reasons; none of those is measured here.

columns.t: State file: pupils, district and the charters it authorised

rows.note: Teacher count as published; it is about 1,000 above the years either side
California reported no staff to the federal file for this year
Federal file not yet published; the State file's "other staff" figure for this year is a fraction of earlier years and looks incomplete

sources.t: U.S. National Center for Education Statistics: Common Core of Data, district directory, membership and staff files, 2014-15 to 2024-25
California Department of Education: staff-to-student ratio files, 2019-20 to 2025-26
